output.question: What are the key takeaways from Anthropic's S-1 filing?

passages.quote: The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock.
The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share.
Our revenue was $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026, up from $1.4 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
Our operating margin was (3)% and operating loss was $567 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026
Because these instruments are marked to market, increases in our enterprise valuation drive increases in this expense.

As of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-term commitments, as well as leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of approximately $900.9 billion, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure.
Additionally, this amount excludes payments under certain other compute and infrastructure arrangements that do not specify a fixed dollar commitment.
We estimate these payments to be in the range of $150 billion to $175 billion .

Through a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors.

Our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors.

output.answer: Anthropic’s November 10 amended S-1 and roadshow announcement set out a proposed Nasdaq “ANT” IPO of 825 million shares at an expected $70–$78 per share. Revenue reached $17.0 billion in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, versus $1.4 billion a year earlier, but Anthropic still recorded a $567 million GAAP operating loss and a −3% operating margin. Its Q3 GAAP net loss was $23.291 billion, with valuation-linked fair-value remeasurement contributing accounting expense. The filing disclosed approximately $900.9 billion of commitments as of and subsequent to September 30—substantially all related to compute and infrastructure—plus an estimated $150–$175 billion under other arrangements excluded from that total. Public shareholders would have limited control: the Long-Term Benefit Trust generally elects a board majority, while the founders’ Class F share would carry 50.1% of voting power on matters submitted to shareholders generally.
caveats: The share count and price range are proposed terms, not a completed IPO; the November 10 announcement said the registration statement had not yet become effective.

The commitments are multi-year obligations, not immediate spending: approximately $70.7 billion is due in the 12 months following September 30, 2026, while approximately $186.2 billion relates to arrangements with termination rights or pre-commencement conditions. The additional $150–$175 billion is an estimate, not a fixed-dollar commitment.
The financial figures cover the quarter ended September 30, 2026. GAAP net loss includes fair-value remeasurement expenses and should not be interpreted as equivalent cash burn.

key_facts.fact: The proposed IPO comprises 825,000,000 Class A shares at an expected $70–$78 per share; Anthropic applied to list on Nasdaq under ANT.
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, revenue was $17.0 billion versus $1.4 billion a year earlier; GAAP operating loss was $567 million and operating margin was −3%.
Q3 2026 GAAP net loss was $23,291 million. The filing explains that increases in enterprise valuation increase the expense from marking certain financing instruments to fair value.

The amended filing reports approximately $900.9 billion of aggregate committed spending as of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, substantially all related to compute and infrastructure; estimated payments of $150–$175 billion under other arrangements are excluded.

Under the proposed post-offering governance structure, the LTBT generally elects and removes directors constituting a board majority, while the Founder LLC’s Class F share carries 50.1% of voting power on matters submitted to shareholders generally.
